html:
The Muscogee (Creek) Nation is the government of the Muscogee people in eastern Oklahoma, with its capital at Okmulgee. This map territory marks their reservation.

In 1492 the ancestors of the Muscogee lived far to the east, in the river towns of present Georgia and Alabama, heirs of the Mississippian chiefdoms that Hernando de Soto passed through in 1540. Their confederacy, the Mvskoke, was a power in the Southeast in the 1700s. Under the Indian Removal Act of 1830 the United States forced them west in the 1830s, a journey that was part of the Trail of Tears. They rebuilt their nation in Indian Territory. In 2020 the US Supreme Court ruled in McGirt v. Oklahoma that their reservation had never been dissolved.
